title: LOKAYAN 2026 - INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI ENTERS PONTA DELGADA, PORTUGAL
body_text:
The Indian Navy’s sail training ship INS Sudarshini entered the port of Ponta Delgada in Azores, Portugal, on 13 Aug 2026 , as part of the ongoing Lokayan 2026 voyage. The arrival marked  successful completion of a challenging 19-day transoceanic passage across the Atlantic Ocean, originating from Boston, USA. This is INS Sudarshini’s second Atlantic crossing , highlighting the endurance, grit and seamanship skills of her crew.
The ship received a warm welcome from the Portuguese Navy on arrival. The port call carries forward the message of India’s rich maritime heritage, friendship and maritime cooperation. During the port call, the Commanding Officer,  INS Sudarshini, called on Comodoro Luís Nicholson Lavrador, Commander of the Azores Maritime Zone (COM CZMA) . The ship will engage in professional interactions, operational replenishment, and cultural exchanges, further strengthening maritime bonds between India and Portugal.
Having traversed over 15,000 nautical miles , INS Sudarshini continues her voyage as a floating ambassador of goodwill and India’s vibrant maritime heritage.

enrichment.summary: INS Sudarshini, the Indian Navy's sail training ship, arrived at Ponta Delgada, Azores (Portugal) on 13 August 2026, completing a 19-day transoceanic Atlantic crossing from Boston, USA, as part of the Lokayan 2026 voyage. This marks the ship's second Atlantic crossing, and it has covered over 15,000 nautical miles so far, engaging in goodwill and cultural exchange activities with the Portuguese Navy.
enrichment.context: INS Sudarshini is a sail training ship of the Indian Navy used to train young officers in traditional seamanship and to project India's maritime heritage abroad through goodwill voyages. Such overseas port calls and long-distance sail voyages are part of India's naval diplomacy efforts, reinforcing bilateral defence and cultural ties with foreign navies, in this case Portugal. These voyages typically have limited direct policy content but reflect India's soft power outreach and 'SAGAR' (Security and Growth for All in the Region) and broader maritime diplomacy themes, and are often covered by PIB primarily as goodwill/public-diplomacy news rather than a policy development.
